# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

---
rp1_run_id: 1d8b87d0-1897-40e6-a1b1-b6aabd8e4736
date: 2026-07-29
status: draft
---

## Overview

This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.

## Context

The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`

### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)

### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`

### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`

### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)

### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer
**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
- Function accepts any valid string input
- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
**As a** developer building a web application
**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs

**Acceptance Scenario**:
- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path

### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
**As a** system processing user-generated content
**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names

**Acceptance Scenario**:
- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use

### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
**As a** developer
**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs

**Acceptance Scenario**:
- **GIVEN** Input contains only special characters like `"!!!@@@###"`
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("!!!@@@###")`
- **THEN** I receive an empty string `""`
- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown

## Constraints

- Function must be a pure function with no side effects
- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
- Empty string input should return empty string output

## Out of Scope

- Transliteration of non-Latin characters (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
- Custom delimiter configuration
- Maximum length truncation
- Duplicate slug detection or versioning
- Database persistence or slug uniqueness validation

## Success Metrics

- All provided examples produce expected output
- Function passes comprehensive test suite covering edge cases
- Function is usable in any part of the codebase requiring text normalization
- Zero runtime errors for any string input

     4→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
     5→
     6→---

    10→---
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
    71→- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`
    72→
    73→### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
    74→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    75→**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
    76→**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
    77→**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
    78→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    79→- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
    80→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
    81→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
    82→- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)
    83→
    84→### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
    85→**Actor**: Developer
    86→**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
    87→**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
    88→**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
    91→- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
    92→- Function accepts any valid string input
    93→- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)
    94→
    95→## User Stories
    96→
    97→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
    98→**As a** developer building a web application
    99→**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
   100→**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs
   101→
   102→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   103→- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
   104→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
   105→- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path
   106→
   107→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content
   109→**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
   110→**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   113→- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
   114→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
   115→- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use
   116→
   117→### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   118→**As a** developer
   119→**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
   120→**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs
   121→
   122→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   123→- **GIVEN** Input contains only special characters like `"!!!@@@###"`
   124→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("!!!@@@###")`
   125→- **THEN** I receive an empty string `""`
   126→- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown
   127→
   128→## Constraints
   129→
   130→- Function must be a pure function with no side effects
   131→- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
   132→- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
   133→- Empty string input should return empty string output
   134→
   135→## Out of Scope
   136→
   137→- Transliteration of non-Latin characters (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   138→- Custom delimiter configuration
   139→- Maximum length truncation
   140→- Duplicate slug detection or versioning
   141→- Database persistence or slug uniqueness validation
   142→
   143→## Success Metrics
   144→
   145→- All provided examples produce expected output

   147→- Function is usable in any part of the codebase requiring text normalization
   148→- Zero runtime errors for any string input

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-29

## Summary

A pure `slugify` function will be added to `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs using a sequential regex-based pipeline: lowercase conversion, whitespace/underscore replacement with hyphens, invalid character removal, hyphen consolidation, and leading/trailing hyphen trimming. This approach follows the existing utility function pattern with no external dependencies, ensuring maximum compatibility and testability.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph src/utils.ts
        slugify["slugify(text: string): string"]
    end

    subgraph Transformation Pipeline
        A[Input Text] --> B[toLowerCase]
        B --> C[Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens]
        C --> D[Remove invalid characters]
        D --> E[Collapse multiple hyphens]
        E --> F[Trim leading/trailing hyphens]
        F --> G[Output Slug]
    end

    slugify --> A
    G --> slugify
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | src/utils.ts | Any importing module | Input: string, Output: string (slug or empty) |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |

    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:

    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`

   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content

1→# Implementation and Release Phases
     2→
     3→Sections §PHASE-3 (implementation, task dispatch, verification aggregation,
     4→readiness) and §PHASE-4 (release and archive). Load once planning completes
     5→and the workflow enters implementation, or when resuming directly into the
     6→implementation or release phase.
     7→
     8→## §PHASE-3: Implementation
     9→
    10→**Skip if**: `START_PHASE` is after `implementation`.
    11→
    12→**Resume checkpoint**: If `WAITING_PHASE.phase == "implementation"`, inspect the latest parent waiting/status event from `WORKFLOW_STATE.recent_events`:
    13→
    14→- `reason = "review_retry_exhausted"` -> resume the repair/skip/stop decision before any new builder dispatch.
    15→- `reason = "readiness_add_task"` or `reason = "release_add_task"` -> run §4.1 against the updated `tasks.json`, then continue implementation from remaining task units.
    16→- `reason = "missing_readiness_contract"` -> jump to §4.6 verification/readiness.
    17→- otherwise jump directly to the Implementation checkpoint if a registered `features/{FEATURE_ID}/build-readiness.md` artifact exists.
    18→
    19→Do not dispatch task-builder, validators, or comment-cleaner before the matching resumed decision path is selected.
    20→
    21→### §4.1 Plan Task Units
    22→
    23→Use the schema-backed task plan sidecar. Do not parse `tasks.md` for machine planning.
    24→
    25→```bash
    26→rp1 agent-tools build-task-plan \
    27→  --tasks-path "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/tasks.json" \
    28→  --max-simple-batch 3 \
    29→  --complex-isolated true
    30→```
    31→
    32→Parse the JSON `ToolResult`.
    33→
    34→- Extract `task_units`, `implementation_tasks`, `documentation_tasks`, and `warnings`.
    35→- Set `TASK_PLAN = data`.
    36→- For each `task_unit`, derive `TASK_UNIT_IDS = task_unit.task_ids.join(",")`. This is the only source for builder/reviewer `TASK_IDS`.
    37→- Preserve `warnings` as `task_plan_warnings` for readiness/release notes.
    38→- If the tool fails or returns malformed output, emit `implementation` waiting with the tool error and STOP. Do not infer task state from markdown.
    39→- If `task_units` is empty, skip task-builder/task-reviewer and continue to documentation follow-ups, cleanup manifest handling, and verification.
    40→
    41→### §4.2 Cleanup Manifest Baseline
    42→
    43→Before the first task-builder unit, snapshot the build-start repository state:
    44→
    45→```bash
    46→rp1 agent-tools change-manifest snapshot \
    47→  --code-root "{codeRoot}" \
    48→  --out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-baseline.json"
    49→```
    50→
    51→Parse the `ToolResult` envelope. On failure: continue the build but record `cleanup_manifest_result` as skipped (`skipReason: "baseline_snapshot_failed"`, `files: 0`, `ownedLineCount: 0`). Do not dispatch `comment-cleaner` later unless `change-manifest generate` explicitly returns `status: "created"` with non-empty ownership.
    52→
    53→### §4.3 Builder-Reviewer Loop
    54→
    55→Process `TASK_PLAN.task_units` via the `schedule-wave` tool. Never derive task IDs from `tasks.md`; use the tool output. Do not edit `tasks.json` from the orchestrator; the reviewer owns task-plan persistence.
    56→
    57→#### Dispatch Cycle
    58→
    59→Track three lists of task IDs across the loop. Unit IDs are renumbered on every call, so never carry a `unit_id` between cycles. Each list holds whole units: record a unit's `task_ids` together, never a subset, or the tool rejects the call as mixed unit state.
    60→
    61→- `COMPLETED_TASK_IDS`: task IDs whose reviewer returned SUCCESS. Starts empty.
    62→- `BUILT_TASK_IDS`: task IDs built **on the primary tree** that no reviewer has accepted yet. Starts empty.
    63→- `PENDING_INTEGRATION_TASK_IDS`: task IDs a secondary builder finished in a worktree that is not yet integrated. Starts empty.
    64→
    65→Every list is passed as a comma-separated string. The tool output gives `task_ids` as JSON arrays, so join them explicitly with `,` -- passing an array literal sends unusable IDs and the tool rejects them.
    66→
    67→Repeat until `schedule-wave` returns an empty `review`, an empty `dispatch`, and an empty `PENDING_INTEGRATION_TASK_IDS`:
    68→
    69→```bash
    70→CLEAN_TREE=$([ -z "$(git -C "{codeRoot}" status --porcelain)" ] && echo true || echo false)
    71→
    72→rp1 agent-tools schedule-wave \
    73→  --tasks-path "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/tasks.json" \
    74→  --completed-task-ids "{COMPLETED_TASK_IDS joined with commas}" \
    75→  --built-task-ids "{BUILT_TASK_IDS joined with commas}" \
    76→  --pending-integration-task-ids "{PENDING_INTEGRATION_TASK_IDS joined with commas}" \
    77→  --max-builders 4 \
    78→  --git-commit {GIT_COMMIT} \
    79→  --clean-tree "$CLEAN_TREE"
    80→```
    81→
    82→Parse the JSON `ToolResult`. Extract `mode`, `review`, `dispatch`, `held`, and `reason`.
    83→
    84→State transitions, which must be applied exactly once per unit:
    85→
    86→- A builder on the primary `codeRoot` that returns successfully adds its unit's `task_ids` to `BUILT_TASK_IDS`.
    87→- A **secondary** builder that returns successfully adds its unit's `task_ids` to `PENDING_INTEGRATION_TASK_IDS`, not `BUILT_TASK_IDS`: its commits are still in the worktree, so the unit can be neither reviewed nor rebuilt. Integration moves those IDs into `BUILT_TASK_IDS`; discarding the worktree removes them from every list so the unit is rebuilt later.
    88→- A reviewer that returns SUCCESS moves its unit's `task_ids` out of `BUILT_TASK_IDS` and into `COMPLETED_TASK_IDS`.
    89→
    90→Units in `review` are already built on the primary tree -- dispatch a reviewer for them, never a builder.
    91→
    92→If `review` and `dispatch` are both empty, use `reason` to decide: `pending_integration` means integrate the outstanding worktrees per `references/parallel-builders.md` and call `schedule-wave` again; `no_ready_units` with uncompleted units remaining is a genuine deadlock, so emit `implementation` waiting with `reason: "dependency_deadlock"` and STOP.
    93→
    94→#### Dispatching from `schedule-wave` Output
    95→
    96→Dispatch every block the tool asks for in ONE message, then wait for all of them. `review[i].task_ids` and `dispatch[i].task_ids` are the only source of `TASK_IDS`. Both are JSON arrays; pass them as a comma-separated string, never as an array literal.
    97→
    98→**Reviewers** -- one block per entry in `review`. Reviewers always run on the primary `codeRoot`:
    99→
   100→Task tool:
   101→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-reviewer
   102→prompt:
   103→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, TASK_IDS={review[i].task_ids joined with commas}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   104→
   105→**Builders** -- one block per entry in `dispatch`. The `primary` entry runs on `codeRoot`:
   106→
   107→Task tool:
   108→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   109→prompt:
   110→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, TASK_IDS={dispatch[i].task_ids joined with commas}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   111→
   112→Each `secondary` entry runs on its own worktree, created per `references/parallel-builders.md` and keyed by that entry's `unit_id`:
   113→
   114→Task tool:
   115→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   116→prompt:
   117→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={worktreePath}, TASK_IDS={dispatch[i].task_ids joined with commas}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   118→
   119→`mode` tells you what the wave contains: `review-only` has no builders, `serial` has exactly one builder -- whether standalone or pipelined alongside a review -- and `parallel-wave` has a primary plus one or more worktree secondaries.
   120→
   121→After every dispatched agent returns, update the three state lists per the Dispatch Cycle rules, integrate any secondary worktrees per `references/parallel-builders.md`, then call `schedule-wave` again. Process reviewer results before integrating.
   122→
   123→#### Reviewer Success
   124→
   125→Reviewer contract: `SUCCESS` + `task_plan_updated = true` completes the unit. Move the unit's `task_ids` out of `BUILT_TASK_IDS` and into `COMPLETED_TASK_IDS`, then call `schedule-wave` again for the next cycle.
   126→
   127→#### Reviewer Failure
   128→
   129→Set `RETRY_TASK_IDS` to the failing unit's `task_ids` and remove them from `BUILT_TASK_IDS` -- the retry rebuilds that unit, so it must not be offered for review again until a builder has re-produced it.
   130→
   131→`attempt = 1`, `max = 2`. On FAILURE with attempt < max: build `PREVIOUS_FEEDBACK` JSON from `issues`/`summary`, re-spawn task-builder with feedback (if `GIT_COMMIT=true`, pass `REWRITE_COMMITS=true`):
   132→
   133→Task tool:
   134→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   135→prompt:
   136→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, TASK_IDS={RETRY_TASK_IDS joined with commas}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, REWRITE_COMMITS={GIT_COMMIT}, PREVIOUS_FEEDBACK={PREVIOUS_FEEDBACK}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   137→
   138→Re-add `RETRY_TASK_IDS` to `BUILT_TASK_IDS` when that builder succeeds, then re-run task-reviewer for the same unit. On second failure, escalate per §4.3.7.
   139→
   140→If another builder was in flight when the reviewer failed: wait for it to finish and record its `task_ids` in `BUILT_TASK_IDS`, but resolve the failed unit's retry before dispatching anything new. The scheduler will offer the waiting unit for review once the failed unit passes. If retry is exhausted, the waiting unit is abandoned alongside it.
   141→
   142→#### Exhausted-Retry Escalation {#s4-3-7}
   143→
   144→Escalate without marking parent `implementation` failed while recovery remains.
   145→
   146→- Interactive: emit `waiting_for_user` on `implementation` with prompt "Task review failed after retry. Repair, Skip task, or Stop?" and context about the failing task unit. Then emit `implementation` waiting with `task_unit: "{RETRY_TASK_IDS}"` and `reason: "review_retry_exhausted"`. STOP with `/build {FEATURE_ID}` resume instructions.
   147→- AFK: if an explicit skip policy exists, record the skipped `RETRY_TASK_IDS` as release follow-ups; otherwise emit parent `implementation` failed only because no skip/repair path remains.
   148→
   149→#### Safety Rules
   150→
   151→1. **Never reviewer and builder on the same unit.** A unit's reviewer dispatches only after that unit's builder completes.
   152→2. **Failure isolation.** When a pipelined reviewer fails, wait for any in-flight builder to finish, then resolve the retry before any new dispatch.
   153→3. **Serial fallback.** When in doubt about preconditions, file overlap, or worktree health, fall back to serial. Parallel-wave is an optimization, not a requirement. The tool may always be called with `--clean-tree false` to force serial mode.
   154→4. **Emit namespacing unchanged.** Both primary and secondary builders emit with the same `task-builder:` step prefix. The `--unit` parameter distinguishes their events.
   155→
   156→See `references/parallel-builders.md` for the full worktree lifecycle protocol: creation, CODE_ROOT routing, integration, conflict fallback, cleanup, and failure handling.
   157→
   158→### §4.4 Post-Build
   159→
   160→Documentation tasks from `TASK_PLAN.documentation_tasks`:
   161→
   162→- Complete only through a declared supported workflow.
   163→- Current build has no declared docs implementation workflow; create `documentation_followups` from each docs task with `id`, `title`, `target`, `acceptance_refs`, `dependencies`, and `blocks_release = false`.
   164→- Carry `documentation_followups` into readiness/release `manual_items`.
   165→- Do not spawn undeclared documentation agents.
   166→
   167→### §4.5 Cleanup Manifest Generation
   168→
   169→After builders, reviewers, and documentation follow-up collection finish, generate the durable cleanup handoff before verification:
   170→
   171→```bash
   172→rp1 agent-tools change-manifest generate \
   173→  --code-root "{codeRoot}" \
   174→  --out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-001.json" \
   175→  --status-out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-status.json" \
   176→  --source build \
   177→  --baseline "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-baseline.json"
   178→```
   179→
   180→Parse the `ToolResult` envelope into `cleanup_manifest_result`. If `data.status == "created"` with `files > 0` and `ownedLineCount > 0`, `comment-cleaner` may participate using `data.manifestPath`. If `data.status == "skipped"`, preserve `statusPath`/`skipReason` for the aggregator. On failure: set skipped with `skipReason: "change_manifest_generate_failed"`, `files: 0`, `ownedLineCount: 0`.
   181→
   182→### §4.6 Verification And Readiness
   183→
   184→#### Step 1 — Resolve comment-cleaner participation
   185→
   186→Evaluate the cleanup manifest result BEFORE dispatching any verification agent. Comment-cleaner participates only when ALL of: `cleanup_manifest_result.data.status == "created"`, `cleanup_manifest_result.data.files > 0`, `cleanup_manifest_result.data.ownedLineCount > 0`, and `cleanup_manifest_result.data.manifestPath` is present. Do not dispatch comment-cleaner with branch, unstaged, commit-range, base-branch, mode, or commit parameters; the generated manifest is the only safe cleanup boundary.
   187→
   188→If comment-cleaner will NOT participate, set the `comment_cleaner` phase result now (before dispatch): `status: "WARN"`, empty `blocking_issues`, one warning noting "Automatic comment cleanup skipped because no non-empty generated manifest was available" with `evidence` from `cleanup_manifest_result.data.statusPath`, one artifact entry for the status path with `storageRoot: "absolute"`, one evidence entry with `status: "not_applicable"` and `summary` from `skipReason`, `files_checked: 0`, `manifest_path: null`, and `manifest_status_path`/`skip_reason` from the cleanup manifest result.
   189→
   190→#### Step 2 — Parallel dispatch
   191→
   192→Emit all dispatch blocks below back-to-back in one message, with no text between them — prose between blocks breaks the parallel dispatch. Always include `code-checker` and `feature-verifier`. Include `comment-cleaner` only when Step 1 resolved it as participating; when not, omit its block entirely. No prose, conditionals, or explanatory text may appear between dispatch blocks.
   193→
   194→Task tool:
   195→subagent_type: rp1-dev:code-checker
   196→prompt:
   197→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}
   198→
   199→Task tool:
   200→subagent_type: rp1-dev:feature-verifier
   201→prompt:
   202→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   203→
   204→Task tool:
   205→subagent_type: rp1-dev:comment-cleaner
   206→prompt:
   207→CHANGE_MANIFEST={cleanup_manifest_result.data.manifestPath}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}
   208→
   209→#### Step 3 — Wait for all before aggregation
   210→
   211→Wait for ALL dispatched verification agents to complete before proceeding. Do not begin aggregation until every agent result is available. Collect each agent's response into its corresponding slot below.
   212→
   213→Build `PHASE_RESULTS_JSON` with keys: `code_checker` (validation envelope or legacy), `feature_verifier` (validation envelope or legacy), `comment_cleaner` (validation envelope or synthetic warning), and `implementation_context` containing `task_plan_warnings` and `documentation_followups` arrays. These MUST be the preserved arrays from §4.1 and §4.4 -- never hardcode to `[]` unless actually empty.
   214→
   215→Task tool:
   216→subagent_type: rp1-dev:build-verify-aggregator
   217→prompt:
   218→PHASE_RESULTS={PHASE_RESULTS_JSON}, FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   219→

   221→
   222→Readiness release behavior:
   223→
   224→- PASS/proceed: release may start.
   225→- WARN/proceed_with_notes: release may start with warnings/manual notes visible.
   226→- FAIL/return_to_implementation: keep parent `implementation` running for planned repair or waiting for a user decision.
   227→- WAITING/wait_for_human: emit parent `implementation` waiting for required manual evidence.
   228→
   229→If readiness has blocking failures or missing required components, keep parent `implementation` running for planned repair or waiting for a user decision. Emit parent `implementation` failed only when no repair/decision path remains.
   230→
   231→If readiness is FAIL or WAITING in interactive mode, present the readiness evidence before stopping: emit `waiting_for_user` on `implementation` with prompt "Readiness needs work. Repair, Add Task, Review feedback from Arcade, or Stop?" and readiness context (status, blocker/warning/manual-item counts, readiness artifact path). Then emit `implementation` waiting with `readiness_status`. STOP with `/build {FEATURE_ID}` resume instructions.

   233→If AFK and readiness is FAIL or WAITING, emit `implementation` failed unless an explicit repair/skip policy is already available.
   234→
   235→When readiness is PASS or WARN and can proceed to release, present the human gate before release.
   236→
   237→**Implementation checkpoint** (after readiness; skip if AFK):
   238→
   239→Emit `waiting_for_user` on `implementation` with prompt "Release, Add Task, Review feedback from Arcade, or Stop?" and readiness context.

STOP with `/build {FEATURE_ID}` resume instructions. On resume, `build-task-plan` must consume the updated `tasks.json`.

   257→After the user chooses Release, or AFK skips this checkpoint, emit `implementation` completed per §PARENT-EMIT-DISCIPLINE table.
   258→
   259→### Git Operations (conditional)
   260→
   261→If GIT_COMMIT: stage+commit. If GIT_PUSH: push. If GIT_PR: create PR.
   262→
   263→## §PHASE-4: Release
   264→
   265→**Skip if**: `START_PHASE` is after `release`.
   266→
   267→**Resume checkpoint**: If `WAITING_PHASE.phase == "release"`, inspect the latest parent waiting/status event from `WORKFLOW_STATE.recent_events`:
   268→
   269→- `reason = "add_task_requested"` -> jump to §PHASE-3 Implementation and consume the updated `tasks.json`.

   277→Before emitting `release` running:

   279→1. Set `READINESS_CONTRACT` from the `build-verify-aggregator` JSON returned in §4.6 when this invocation ran implementation.

     5→
     6→---

    10→---
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
    71→- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`
    72→
    73→### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
    74→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    75→**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
    76→**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
    77→**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
    78→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    79→- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
    80→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
    81→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
    82→- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)
    83→
    84→### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
    85→**Actor**: Developer
    86→**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
    87→**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
    88→**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
    91→- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
    92→- Function accepts any valid string input
    93→- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)
    94→
    95→## User Stories
    96→
    97→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
    98→**As a** developer building a web application
    99→**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
   100→**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs
   101→
   102→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   103→- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
   104→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
   105→- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path
   106→
   107→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content
   109→**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
   110→**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   113→- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
   114→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
   115→- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use
   116→
   117→### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   118→**As a** developer
   119→**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
   120→**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs
   121→
   122→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   123→- **GIVEN** Input contains only special characters like `"!!!@@@###"`
   124→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("!!!@@@###")`
   125→- **THEN** I receive an empty string `""`
   126→- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown
   127→
   128→## Constraints
   129→
   130→- Function must be a pure function with no side effects
   131→- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
   132→- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
   133→- Empty string input should return empty string output

     2→rp1_doc_id: 88d862a3-a705-4269-8a01-5de66ae50017
     3→---
     4→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
     5→
     6→---
     7→rp1_run_id: 1d8b87d0-1897-40e6-a1b1-b6aabd8e4736
     8→date: 2026-07-29
     9→status: draft
    10→---
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
    71→- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`
    72→
    73→### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
    74→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    75→**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
    76→**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
    77→**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
    78→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    79→- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
    80→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
    81→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
    82→- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)
    83→
    84→### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
    85→**Actor**: Developer
    86→**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
    87→**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
    88→**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
    91→- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
    92→- Function accepts any valid string input
    93→- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)
    94→
    95→## User Stories
    96→
    97→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
    98→**As a** developer building a web application
    99→**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
   100→**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs
   101→
   102→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   103→- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
   104→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
   105→- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path
   106→
   107→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content
   109→**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
   110→**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   113→- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
   114→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
   115→- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use
   116→
   117→### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   118→**As a** developer
   119→**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
   120→**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs
   121→
   122→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   123→- **GIVEN** Input contains only special characters like `"!!!@@@###"`
   124→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("!!!@@@###")`
   125→- **THEN** I receive an empty string `""`
   126→- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown
   127→
   128→## Constraints
   129→
   130→- Function must be a pure function with no side effects
   131→- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
   132→- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
   133→- Empty string input should return empty string output
   134→
   135→## Out of Scope
   136→
   137→- Transliteration of non-Latin characters (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   138→- Custom delimiter configuration
   139→- Maximum length truncation
   140→- Duplicate slug detection or versioning
   141→- Database persistence or slug uniqueness validation
   142→
   143→## Success Metrics
   144→
   145→- All provided examples produce expected output
   146→- Function passes comprehensive test suite covering edge cases
   147→- Function is usable in any part of the codebase requiring text normalization
   148→- Zero runtime errors for any string input
   149→
   150→## AFK Mode Processing Notes
   151→
   152→This requirements document was generated in AFK mode with the following automated decisions:
   153→
   154→### Decision Log

   156→| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |

   158→| PRD Selection | None | No PRDs found in `.rp1/work/prds/`; project charter unavailable. Proceeding based on inline requirements and KB context. |
   159→| Character Set Scope | Letters, numbers, hyphens only | Conservative interpretation of "not a letter, number, or hyphen" ensures maximum URL and filesystem compatibility. |
   160→| Unicode Handling | Accept Unicode letters/numbers | TypeScript/JavaScript regex character classes naturally handle Unicode; no explicit restriction stated. |
   161→| Empty Input Handling | Return empty string | Most conservative and safe default; avoids null/undefined complications. |
   162→| Function Location | `src/utils.ts` | KB indicates utility functions belong in this module; follows existing project pattern. |
   163→| Test Coverage | Comprehensive suite required | Success metric explicitly requires test suite; aligns with existing `utils.test.ts` pattern. |
   164→
   165→### Inferred Constraints
   166→
   167→- **Performance**: No specific requirements stated; assuming typical string utility performance standards (sub-millisecond for strings under 1KB)
   168→- **Error Handling**: No exceptions for invalid input specified; function will gracefully handle all string inputs
   169→- **Integration**: Function must be callable from any module; standard ES module export assumed

# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility

---
rp1_run_id: 1d8b87d0-1897-40e6-a1b1-b6aabd8e4736
date: 2026-07-29
status: draft
---

## Overview

This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.

## Context

The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`

### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)

### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`

### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`

### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer or system component
**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)

### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
**Actor**: Developer
**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
- Function accepts any valid string input
- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
**As a** developer building a web application
**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs

**Acceptance Scenario**:
- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path

### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
**As a** system processing user-generated content
**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names

**Acceptance Scenario**:
- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use

### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
**As a** developer
**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs

**Acceptance Scenario**:
- **GIVEN** Input contains only special characters like `"!!!@@@###"`
- **WHEN** I call `slugify("!!!@@@###")`
- **THEN** I receive an empty string `""`
- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown

## Constraints

- Function must be a pure function with no side effects
- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
- Empty string input should return empty string output

## Out of Scope

- Transliteration of non-Latin characters (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
- Custom delimiter configuration
- Maximum length truncation
- Duplicate slug detection or versioning
- Database persistence or slug uniqueness validation

## Success Metrics

- All provided examples produce expected output
- Function passes comprehensive test suite covering edge cases
- Function is usable in any part of the codebase requiring text normalization
- Zero runtime errors for any string input

# Design: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-29

## Summary

A pure `slugify` function will be added to `src/utils.ts` that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs using a sequential regex-based pipeline: lowercase conversion, whitespace/underscore replacement with hyphens, invalid character removal, hyphen consolidation, and leading/trailing hyphen trimming. This approach follows the existing utility function pattern with no external dependencies, ensuring maximum compatibility and testability.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph src/utils.ts
        slugify["slugify(text: string): string"]
    end

    subgraph Transformation Pipeline
        A[Input Text] --> B[toLowerCase]
        B --> C[Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens]
        C --> D[Remove invalid characters]
        D --> E[Collapse multiple hyphens]
        E --> F[Trim leading/trailing hyphens]
        F --> G[Output Slug]
    end

    slugify --> A
    G --> slugify
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | src/utils.ts | Any importing module | Input: string, Output: string (slug or empty) |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Pure function implementing text-to-slug transformation via regex pipeline | src/utils.ts |
| T2 | slugify tests | Comprehensive test suite covering all requirements and edge cases | src/utils.test.ts |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Core implementation has no dependencies

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface dependency: tests import and call the slugify function)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| Lowercase conversion (REQ-001) | Uppercase characters in output | unit | `bun test` |
| Whitespace/underscore replacement (REQ-002) | Spaces or underscores in output | unit | `bun test` |
| Invalid character removal (REQ-003) | Special characters in output | unit | `bun test` |
| Hyphen consolidation (REQ-004) | Multiple consecutive hyphens | unit | `bun test` |
| Leading/trailing trim (REQ-005) | Output starts/ends with hyphen | unit | `bun test` |
| Composite transformation (REQ-006) | Combined edge cases fail | unit | `bun test` |
| Empty/invalid input handling | Errors or unexpected output | unit | `bun test` |
| Function signature (REQ-007) | Incorrect export or signature | unit | TypeScript compilation + import test |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | .rp1/context/modules.md | Utils section | modules.md:Utils | Add slugify to documented utility functions |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Unicode edge cases with certain character classes | LOW | Regex pattern explicitly targets a-z, 0-9, hyphens; non-matching chars removed. Transliteration explicitly out of scope. |

# Design Decisions: Slugify Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-29

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Implementation location | src/utils.ts | Follows existing pattern for utility functions; KB modules.md specifies utils.ts for reusable utilities | New file src/slugify.ts (rejected: unnecessary file proliferation for single function) |
| D2 | Transformation approach | Sequential regex pipeline | Simple, readable, testable; each step is a single regex replace operation | State machine parser (rejected: overcomplicated for this use case); External library (rejected: KB patterns.md specifies no external dependencies) |
| D3 | Character set for valid output | a-z, 0-9, hyphen only | Matches requirements; ensures maximum URL/filesystem compatibility | Extended ASCII (rejected: requirements specify letters/numbers/hyphens only) |
| D4 | Empty input handling | Return empty string | Requirements specify graceful handling; most conservative approach | Throw error (rejected: requirements want no exceptions); Return placeholder like "untitled" (rejected: not specified in requirements) |
| D5 | Unicode letter handling | Remove non-ASCII letters | Requirements explicitly exclude transliteration; simpler implementation | Transliterate to ASCII equivalents (rejected: explicitly out of scope) |
| D6 | Test structure | Extend existing utils.test.ts | Follows existing co-located test pattern with describe/test/expect | Separate slugify.test.ts (rejected: doesn't match existing pattern for utils.ts) |

---

| Language/Runtime | TypeScript on Bun | KB index.md, codebase | Project uses Bun/TypeScript stack |
| Module location | src/utils.ts | KB modules.md | Utility functions belong in utils module |
| Test framework | bun:test | KB patterns.md, codebase | Existing test pattern uses Bun built-in test runner |
| Export style | Named export | Codebase (utils.ts) | Existing functions use `export function` pattern |
| Documentation style | JSDoc comment | Codebase (utils.ts) | Existing functions have JSDoc-style doc comments |
| Function naming | camelCase (slugify) | KB patterns.md | Functions use camelCase per project convention |

     4→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
     5→
     6→---
     7→rp1_run_id: 1d8b87d0-1897-40e6-a1b1-b6aabd8e4736
     8→date: 2026-07-29

    10→---
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
    71→- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`
    72→
    73→### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
    74→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    75→**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
    76→**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
    77→**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
    78→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    79→- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
    80→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
    81→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
    82→- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)
    83→
    84→### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
    85→**Actor**: Developer
    86→**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
    87→**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
    88→**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
    91→- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
    92→- Function accepts any valid string input
    93→- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)
    94→
    95→## User Stories
    96→
    97→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
    98→**As a** developer building a web application
    99→**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
   100→**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs
   101→
   102→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   103→- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
   104→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
   105→- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path
   106→
   107→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content
   109→**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
   110→**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   113→- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
   114→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
   115→- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use
   116→
   117→### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   118→**As a** developer
   119→**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
   120→**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs
   121→
   122→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   123→- **GIVEN** Input contains only special characters like `"!!!@@@###"`
   124→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("!!!@@@###")`
   125→- **THEN** I receive an empty string `""`
   126→- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown
   127→
   128→## Constraints
   129→
   130→- Function must be a pure function with no side effects
   131→- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
   132→- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
   133→- Empty string input should return empty string output
   134→
   135→## Out of Scope
   136→
   137→- Transliteration of non-Latin characters (e.g., converting "café" to "cafe")
   138→- Custom delimiter configuration
   139→- Maximum length truncation
   140→- Duplicate slug detection or versioning
   141→- Database persistence or slug uniqueness validation
   142→

   147→- Function is usable in any part of the codebase requiring text normalization
   148→- Zero runtime errors for any string input

     4→# Feature Requirements: Slugify Utility
     5→
     6→---
