    10→---
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
    71→- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`
    72→
    73→### REQ-006: Composite Transformation [MUST HAVE]
    74→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    75→**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
    76→**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
    77→**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
    78→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    79→- Input `"  Foo__Bar  "` produces `"foo-bar"` (spaces, underscores, and edge hyphens handled)
    80→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (punctuation removed, spaces replaced)
    81→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"` (hyphens collapsed)
    82→- Input `"!!!@@@###"` produces `""` (only invalid chars results in empty string)
    83→
    84→### REQ-007: Function Interface [MUST HAVE]
    85→**Actor**: Developer
    86→**Action**: Call a function named `slugify` with a single string parameter
    87→**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
    88→**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component
    89→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    90→- Function signature is `slugify(text: string): string`
    91→- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
    92→- Function accepts any valid string input
    93→- Function returns a string (may be empty if input contains no valid characters)
    94→
    95→## User Stories
    96→
    97→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
    98→**As a** developer building a web application
    99→**I want** to convert article titles or user input into URL slugs
   100→**So that** I can create clean, readable, and SEO-friendly URLs
   101→
   102→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   103→- **GIVEN** I have a blog post titled "Hello, World! My First Post"
   104→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Hello, World! My First Post")`
   105→- **THEN** I receive `"hello-world-my-first-post"` suitable for URL path
   106→
   107→### STORY-002: Normalize Identifiers from User Input
   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content
   109→**I want** to convert arbitrary text into safe identifiers
   110→**So that** I can use them as filenames, database keys, or CSS class names
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Scenario**:
   113→- **GIVEN** A user enters "Project #1: Design & Dev!!!" as a project name
   114→- **WHEN** I call `slugify("Project #1: Design & Dev!!!")`
   115→- **THEN** I receive `"project-1-design-dev"` safe for filesystem and database use
   116→
   117→### STORY-003: Handle Edge Cases Gracefully
   118→**As a** developer
   119→**I want** the slugify function to handle empty, whitespace-only, or special-character-only input
   120→**So that** my application doesn't crash or produce invalid slugs
   121→
   122→**Acceptance Scenario**:

   126→- **AND** no errors or exceptions are thrown
   127→
   128→## Constraints

   131→- Must handle Unicode letters and numbers appropriately
   132→- Performance should be reasonable for typical text inputs (up to several hundred characters)
   133→- Empty string input should return empty string output

    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→This feature provides a text transformation utility function that converts arbitrary strings into URL-friendly slugs. The utility normalizes input text by converting to lowercase, replacing whitespace and underscores with hyphens, removing invalid characters, and ensuring a clean hyphen-delimited format suitable for URLs, filenames, and identifiers.
    15→
    16→## Context
    17→
    18→The rp1-eval-project is a utility scripting project built with Bun and TypeScript. The slugify utility will be added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module as a pure function, following the project's established pattern for reusable utility logic.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    23→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    24→**Action**: Convert any input text string to lowercase
    25→**Outcome**: All alphabetic characters in the output are lowercase
    26→**Rationale**: URL slugs conventionally use lowercase to avoid case-sensitivity issues in different systems and ensure consistency across platforms
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces output starting with `"hello"`
    29→- Input `"UPPERCASE"` produces `"uppercase"`
    30→- Input `"MixedCase123"` produces `"mixedcase123"`
    31→
    32→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    33→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    34→**Action**: Replace all spaces and underscores with single hyphens
    35→**Outcome**: No spaces or underscores remain in the output; they are replaced by hyphens
    36→**Rationale**: URLs cannot contain spaces, and hyphens are the standard delimiter for multi-word slugs, improving readability and SEO
    37→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    38→- Input `"Hello World"` produces `"hello-world"`
    39→- Input `"Foo__Bar"` produces `"foo-bar"` (multiple underscores become single hyphen)
    40→- Input `"one two three"` produces `"one-two-three"`
    41→
    42→### REQ-003: Invalid Character Removal [MUST HAVE]
    43→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    44→**Action**: Remove any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen
    45→**Outcome**: Output contains only alphanumeric characters and hyphens
    46→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs and filesystems; restricting to alphanumerics and hyphens ensures maximum compatibility
    47→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    48→- Input `"Hello, World!"` produces `"hello-world"` (comma and exclamation removed)
    49→- Input `"test@email.com"` produces `"testemailcom"` (@ and . removed)
    50→- Input `"a+b=c"` produces `"abc"` (operators removed)
    51→
    52→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation [MUST HAVE]
    53→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    54→**Action**: Collapse sequences of multiple hyphens into a single hyphen
    55→**Outcome**: No consecutive hyphens appear in the output
    56→**Rationale**: Multiple hyphens reduce readability and can cause issues with some URL parsers; single hyphens provide clean word separation
    57→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    58→- Input `"a---b"` produces `"a-b"`
    59→- Input `"foo--bar"` produces `"foo-bar"`
    60→- Input `"test----case"` produces `"test-case"`
    61→
    62→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
    63→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    64→**Action**: Remove hyphens from the beginning and end of the output string
    65→**Outcome**: Output does not start or end with a hyphen
    66→**Rationale**: Leading and trailing hyphens are semantically meaningless in slugs and can cause parsing issues in routing systems
    67→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    68→- Input `"-hello-"` produces `"hello"`
    69→- Input `"--start"` produces `"start"`
    70→- Input `"end--"` produces `"end"`
    71→- Input `"-both-"` produces `"both"`
    72→

    74→**Actor**: Developer or system component
    75→**Action**: Apply all normalization rules in sequence to produce a valid slug
    76→**Outcome**: Any arbitrary text input produces a clean, valid slug or empty string
    77→**Rationale**: Real-world text requires coordinated application of all rules to handle edge cases consistently
    78→**Acceptance Criteria**:

    83→

    85→**Actor**: Developer

    87→**Outcome**: Function returns a string containing the transformed slug
    88→**Rationale**: Simple, predictable API enables easy integration into any codebase component

    91→- Function is exported from `src/utils.ts` module
    92→- Function accepts any valid string input

    95→## User Stories
    96→
    97→### STORY-001: Generate URL-Friendly Slugs
    98→**As a** developer building a web application

   108→**As a** system processing user-generated content
